text: Q: When is rent due and how can a resident pay? A: Rent is due on the 1st of each month. There is a grace period through the 5th; rent received after the 5th is late. Residents can pay through the Mira resident portal by bank transfer or card, or enroll in AutoPay to have rent drawn automatically on the 1st. Always quote the resident's exact balance and due date from their account record; never estimate an amount.

Q: What is the late fee policy? A: If rent is not received by the end of the grace period on the 5th, a late fee of 50 dollars applies, plus 10 dollars per day after the 10th, up to a cap of 100 dollars per month. A first-time late fee may be waived once per 12 months for residents in good standing. Late rent that remains unpaid past the 10th may begin the notice process per the lease and local law.

Q: How does a resident submit a maintenance request? A: Routine maintenance requests (a dripping faucet, a loose handle, an appliance issue) are logged as a work order and a technician is scheduled, typically within two to three business days. Describe the issue and the location in the unit. For anything urgent or after hours, see the emergency policy. Mira confirms every work order by text with a tracking number.

Q: What counts as a maintenance emergency and what should a resident do? A: Emergencies are issues that threaten safety or cause active property damage: a major water leak or flooding, no heat in freezing weather, a gas smell, a total power outage, an overflowing sewage backup, or being locked out. For a gas smell, leave the unit immediately and call the gas company and 911 first, then Mira. For a water leak, shut off the water at the valve and report it as an emergency so a technician is dispatched right away rather than scheduled. Emergencies are handled 24/7.

Q: Where is the water shutoff and how do you stop a leak? A: Each unit has a main water shutoff valve, usually under the kitchen sink or near the water heater; turn it clockwise to stop the flow. Individual fixtures have their own shutoff valves behind or below them. For a leak, shut off the nearest valve first to limit damage, move belongings away from the water, and report it as an emergency work order so a technician is dispatched.

Q: Who is responsible for repairs, the landlord or the resident? A: The landlord is responsible for maintaining the structure, plumbing, electrical, heating, and supplied appliances in working order, and for habitability. The resident is responsible for damage they or their guests cause beyond normal wear and tear, for keeping the unit clean, and for replacing consumables like light bulbs and smoke-detector batteries. When responsibility is unclear, log the work order and Mira will assess on site; charges only apply for resident-caused damage and are disclosed first.

Q: How does the security deposit work and when is it returned? A: The security deposit is held for the term of the lease. After move-out, it is returned within the period required by local law (commonly 14 to 30 days) minus any lawful deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear. Normal wear and tear cannot be deducted. An itemized statement of any deductions is provided with the refund. Cleaning and painting for ordinary use are generally the landlord's cost, not deductions.

Q: How does lease renewal work? A: Mira sends a renewal offer about 60 days before the lease end date. A resident can renew for another term, switch to month-to-month where offered (often at a higher rate), or give notice to vacate. If no action is taken by the lease end, the lease may convert to month-to-month per its terms. Any rent change at renewal is stated in the offer and is subject to local rent regulations where they apply.

Q: Can a resident break their lease early? A: Breaking a lease early generally requires written notice and may involve an early-termination fee or responsibility for rent until the unit is re-rented, as stated in the lease. Some situations are protected by law (for example active military deployment, or unsafe/uninhabitable conditions) and may allow termination without penalty. Mira will work with the resident on options such as a lease transfer or finding a replacement resident.

Q: What is the policy on subletting and long-term guests? A: Subletting requires prior written approval from Mira; the proposed subtenant must apply and be screened, and the original resident usually remains responsible under the lease. Guests staying longer than 14 consecutive days may be considered unauthorized occupants and must be added to the lease. Short visits are fine and need no approval.

Q: What are the community rules around noise, pets, and parking? A: Quiet hours are 10 PM to 7 AM; keep noise low so it does not disturb neighbors. Pets require an approved pet addendum and any applicable pet deposit or rent; service and assistance animals are not pets and are accommodated per law. Each unit has its assigned parking space or permit; guest parking is in marked visitor spots only, and unauthorized vehicles may be towed.

Q: What is the move-out process? A: Give written notice per the lease (commonly 30 to 60 days before the end date). Schedule a move-out inspection, return all keys and remotes, and leave the unit broom-clean with personal belongings removed. The security deposit, minus any lawful deductions, is returned with an itemized statement within the legally required window. Forwarding address should be provided so the refund can be sent.

Q: How do I get help after office hours? A: The leasing office is open Monday to Friday, 9 AM to 5 PM. Outside those hours, weekends, and holidays, you can still reach Mira 24/7 by phone or text for questions and to report issues. Emergencies are handled immediately around the clock. Non-emergency requests submitted after hours are logged right away and scheduled the next business day, so nothing falls through the cracks.

Q: What is an after-hours emergency and what should I do? A: For anything life-threatening or a gas leak, call 911 first. Property emergencies handled 24/7 include a major water leak or flooding, no heat in freezing weather, no power to the whole unit, a sewage backup, a broken exterior door or lock that is a security risk, or being locked out. Report these right away and an on-call technician is dispatched immediately. Routine issues like a dripping faucet, a squeaky door, or a single light out are not emergencies and are scheduled during business hours.

Q: I am locked out after hours, what do I do? A: Report a lockout and the on-call team will arrange access to your unit. Have ID ready to verify you are a resident. An after-hours lockout service fee may apply per your lease. For your safety, do not try to force a door or window or climb in; wait for the on-call team.

Q: A neighbor is being loud late at night, what can I do? A: Quiet hours are 10 PM to 7 AM. For an after-hours noise disturbance, note the date and time and report it; management follows up the next business day and repeated violations are addressed per the lease. If you ever feel unsafe, or it looks like a domestic or violent disturbance, call 911 first.

Q: The power, water, or heat went out after hours. A: First check whether it affects just your unit or the whole building, and check your breaker panel for a tripped breaker. A building-wide outage is often a utility-company issue; report it and management will coordinate with the provider. Loss of heat in freezing weather, no running water, or a full power outage in your unit is treated as an after-hours emergency and a technician is dispatched right away.

Q: There is mold in my apartment, what should I do? A: First ask ONE clarifying question to size it up: roughly how large is the affected area — smaller or larger than about one square foot (a sheet of paper) — and what surface is it on? For a SMALL patch (under about one square foot) on a hard, non-porous surface like tile, grout, or a painted wall, the resident can usually handle it: put on gloves, wipe the area with a mix of dish soap and warm water (or a solution of one part bleach to ten parts water on non-porous surfaces only), dry it completely, then keep the area dry and improve airflow by running the bathroom or kitchen fan and reducing humidity. Tell them to follow up if it comes back. If the resident says that remedy did not work, or the mold is larger than about one square foot, keeps returning, is on porous material like drywall or carpet, or there are health concerns, do NOT have them keep cleaning it — create a maintenance work order and dispatch the on-call team, which is available 24/7 including overnight, because persistent or spreading mold is a health and habitability issue.

Q: My toilet or sink is clogged. A: Try to clear it first. For a clogged toilet, do not keep flushing (it can overflow); use a flange plunger, make a tight seal, and plunge firmly several times, then test with a small flush. For a slow sink or tub, remove and clean the stopper and hair from the drain and try a cup plunger; a mix of hot water with a little dish soap can help grease clogs. Avoid chemical drain cleaners, which can damage pipes. If plunging does not clear it, water is backing up, or it is a sewage backup, create a maintenance work order so a plumber is sent out.

Q: My garbage disposal stopped working or is jammed. A: First, never put your hand inside it. If it hums but doesn't spin or is silent: turn the disposal switch OFF, then press the small red RESET button on the underside of the unit and try again. If it only hums, it's jammed — with the power off, use the hex/Allen wrench in the slot at the bottom center to turn the blades free, then hit reset. If it still won't run after resetting, create a maintenance work order so a technician can take a look.

Q: I have no hot water. A: Quick checks first: make sure the issue isn't just a faucet set to cold, and check whether other taps also lack hot water. If you have an electric water heater, check the breaker panel for a tripped breaker and reset it. If it's gas and the pilot light is out and you know how to relight it safely, follow the instructions on the unit — but if you smell gas, leave and call 911 and the gas company first. If there's still no hot water after these checks, create a maintenance work order; total loss of hot water is treated as urgent and dispatched promptly.

Q: Some of my outlets or lights went out. A: This is usually a tripped breaker or GFCI outlet. At the breaker panel, find any breaker that's in the middle or OFF position, flip it fully OFF and then back ON. In kitchens, bathrooms, garages, and outdoors, also check for a GFCI outlet with a RESET button and press it. If a breaker trips again right after resetting, stop — that points to an electrical fault; unplug devices on that circuit and create a maintenance work order so an electrician can check it.

Q: My AC or heat isn't working well. A: First check the thermostat — confirm it's set to COOL or HEAT and the temperature is set past the current room temperature, and replace the batteries if the screen is blank. Then check and replace a dirty air filter, which is the most common cause of weak airflow, and make sure vents aren't blocked. Give it a few minutes to respond. If it still won't cool or heat after these steps — or there's no heat in freezing weather, which is an emergency — create a maintenance work order so an HVAC technician is dispatched.
